items.facebook_caption:
How long does it take to build a website in Singapore? ⏱️

A standard business site takes 1–2 weeks once your content is ready. Larger or custom builds with more pages, features or integrations take 6–8 weeks.

The biggest factor is rarely design or coding. It's how quickly content and decisions move. To stay on schedule:
✅ Have your text, photos and logo ready on day one
✅ Nominate one person to approve feedback
✅ Save "can we also add…" ideas for phase 2

Full guide, including what to prepare 👇
https://www.adssentialmarketing.com/how-long-to-build-a-website-singapore/

#WebDesignSingapore #SmallBusinessSG #WebsiteTips

items.facebook_caption:
Custom website or template: which does your business need? 🧩

A template suits a business that needs a credible, standard site fast. A custom website is worth it when the site must do something specific: special features, integrations, a distinct brand or big growth plans.

Many Singapore SMEs do best with the middle path: a well-customised theme.

Full comparison, with the hidden costs of templates 👇
https://www.adssentialmarketing.com/custom-website-vs-template/

#WebDesignSingapore #WordPress #SmallBusinessSG

items.facebook_caption:
Does your website need an llms.txt file? 🤔

llms.txt is a 2024 proposal, not an official standard. Google ignores it, and no major AI company says it relies on one, so treat it as optional.

What matters more for AI search today: your robots.txt settings, and clear pages that answer customers' questions directly.

Full breakdown before you pay anyone to set one up 👇
https://www.adssentialmarketing.com/what-is-llms-txt/

#GEO #AISearch #SEOSingapore

WordPress, Shopify, Wix, Webflow or Squarespace? 🖥️

For most Singapore service businesses, self-hosted WordPress is the most flexible long-term choice. Shopify suits product-led online shops, Wix and Squarespace suit owners who want to build it themselves, and Webflow suits design-led sites with a capable team.

Side-by-side costs and Singapore notes for each 👇
